lines: {target}? Strange quiet can make a place feel too safe.
If anyone heads for Mushroom Fields, this is my advice. Eat only what you know and keep your boat close.
Mycelium underfoot is not village dirt.
Mushroom Fields is no small story.
I will remember Mushroom Fields as odd land where even the grass changed its mind.
I would mark down my route before going anywhere near Mushroom Fields.
Before Mushroom Fields, I would count my food and test every torch.
Stillness can hide trouble, so I would stay alert inside Mushroom Fields.
Bring home the story and leave the scratches at Mushroom Fields.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Mushroom Fields.
Knowing about mycelium and giant mushrooms standing without hostile crowds, I would avoid turning a peaceful island into a work yard.
Before I followed that route, I would set aside a gentle shovel and an axe for mushroom stems.
Open ground with nowhere to hide is the sort of trouble that punishes a rushed repair.
A repair can wait until the road kept in sight is clear.
The open ground across Mushroom Fields sounds like a place for a light pack and tools tied down tight.
I could build better gear for the next trip if I saw where this set wore down around Mushroom Fields.
Surviving Mushroom Fields does not make a tool sound. Let me inspect it before the next trip.
After hearing that story about Mushroom Fields, I would give everyone one useful tool. Then nobody has to carry the whole workshop.
That story changes what I would put in the pack for Mushroom Fields.
There is no shame in turning back when the repair kit starts looking too small around Mushroom Fields.
{target}? Open ground shows you to everything else.
If anyone heads for Plains, this is my advice. Keep moving and watch the horizon.
Grass bends before trouble arrives if you look.
Plains is no small story.
I will remember Plains as wide land with nowhere to hide after dark.
Someone should know my return path before I head toward Plains.
A clear head is worth more than one extra tool around Plains.
I would pay closest attention when nothing seemed wrong in Plains.
Coming back safely would be enough reward for visiting Plains.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Plains.
The part about open grass making weather and travelers visible from far away is enough reason to use the clear sightlines to plan the route.
There is no good time for a handle to split, especially around open ground with nowhere to hide.
If a threat crossing the grass showed up, I wouldn't want a cracked handle between me and the road kept in sight.
If an open-country storm came early, I would pack the tools and keep moving.
Keep the tools rolled up at a low wall until the way to the road kept in sight is clear.
There is room in my pack for a spare grip if the road leads to Plains.
At Plains, one bent pick can be fixed. A whole pack lost to carelessness cannot.
What did you put on the repair bench first after Plains?
For another trip to Plains, if the route demands climbing, every tool gets a tie before it gets packed.
At Plains, I would keep the repair kit where I could reach it without emptying the pack.
{target}? Sunny fields can still point toward trouble.
If anyone heads for Sunflower Plains, this is my advice. Enjoy the flowers with a torch ready.
Sunflowers face light, not safety.
Sunflower Plains is no small story.
I will remember Sunflower Plains as bright fields that still grow dark at night.
A journey to Sunflower Plains starts with leaving clear directions at home.
A sensible load for Sunflower Plains starts with food and dependable torches.
Silence would be another reason to move carefully through Sunflower Plains.
The village needs returning travelers more than trophies from Sunflower Plains.
<shake>Pride</shake> makes a poor repair kit when things go wrong at Sunflower Plains.
I would make room for a clean hoe and a small repair kit before setting out for Sunflower Plains.
The pack can hold the spares. My dependable tool stays out while a threat crossing the grass could trap us.
I would oil and wrap the iron before trusting it to an open-country storm.
I would keep spare blocks ready along the road kept in sight. Paths fail too.
I would test my footing on the open ground across Sunflower Plains before swinging anything heavy.
What broke at Sunflower Plains, and what did you wish you had packed instead?
I can fit tools for Sunflower Plains. I cannot forge good judgment for the person carrying them.
Come to my bench before another trip to Sunflower Plains. I want to correct whatever gave you trouble.
For another trip to Sunflower Plains, a clean edge helps, but a secure handle gets you home.
I would rather carry a spare handle than limp home from Sunflower Plains with a useless tool.
